title: Generated-header dependency identity bridge
hypothesis: A manifest emitter can create stale downstream artifacts when it declares a generated header by a relative path while the compiler reports the same header by an absolute path.
why_hard: Diagnosis crosses the generator declaration, compiler dependency metadata, and scheduler path identity. A force-rebuild workaround can restore the final payload while violating the incremental-work contract.
next_action: Revisit after the actual Ninja screen only if a realistic original emitter and failure chain can be justified; verify across fresh roots, path spellings, no-op builds, and unrelated-input changes.

sources.note: Recorded primary discussion of absolute compiler depfile paths versus relative manifest paths for generated headers.
Recorded production remedy supports the identity invariant and creates direct-solution lookup risk.

notes: Earlier build research preferred this prototype; the active harder screen instead prioritizes real Ninja scheduler source. Parking preserves the alternative and its rationale. No fixture or model outcome is established by this record.
